neighborhoods.name: Eastside Historic District
neighborhoods.character: Historic parkway mansions, grand colonials, and tree-lined residential avenues adjacent to Eastside Park
neighborhoods.description: Historic residential district developed during Paterson's silk manufacturing boom, featuring grand residences and historic district preservation standards.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Higher assessed values contribute disproportionate residential share to municipal levy.

neighborhoods.name: South Paterson (Little Istanbul & Arab Quarter)
neighborhoods.character: Vibrant commercial artery along Main St with dense two-family and multi-family residential side streets
neighborhoods.description: Culinary and cultural heart of Paterson's Middle Eastern and Turkish community, with mixed-use ground floor commercial ratables supporting high-density residences.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High rental concentration where property tax increases are directly passed through to residential tenant rents.

neighborhoods.name: Hillcrest & Westside
neighborhoods.character: Elevated single-family and duplex residential neighborhood bordering Totowa and Passaic County Community College
neighborhoods.description: Stable residential neighborhood bordering western suburban towns, featuring post-war cape cods and colonials on modest suburban lots.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Core homeowner base bearing steady property tax escalation without commercial ratable buffers.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown & Commercial Core
neighborhoods.character: Civic center, City Hall, Passaic County Courthouse complex, transit terminal, and urban mixed-use apartments
neighborhoods.description: Downtown commercial and government core featuring historic loft conversions and high-density apartment properties.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Subject to commercial tax appeals and PILOT redevelopment abatements.

neighborhoods.name: Northside & Haledon Border
neighborhoods.character: Hilly terrain overlooking Great Falls National Historical Park, mix of single-family homes and multi-family dwellings
neighborhoods.description: Historic residential neighborhood situated above the Passaic River gorge, providing entry-level homeownership and multi-generational rental housing.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Sensitive to municipal sewer and water rate shifts and county equalized tax rates.

neighborhoods.name: Sandy Hill & People's Park
neighborhoods.character: Dense urban neighborhood near Route 19 and 21, multi-family frame dwellings and local bodegas
neighborhoods.description: High-density residential neighborhood with deep industrial heritage, housing working families and essential service workers.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Extreme tax burden as percentage of household income, exceeding 18% in lower brackets.

equityAnalysis.summary: Paterson City maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Paterson City, homeowners pay an average of $9,320.25 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 18.72% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 45.38%, assessed values average ~45.38% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 36.8% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 46.2%, and Passaic County claims 17.0%.
